newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Pru making progress on SIB review.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Pru making progress on SIB review.

text.p: Prudential Corp on Wednesday said it had made huge progress on its pension misselling review over the last two months.

Speaking after the life insurance giant announced it was increasing provisions for the review by over 200 million pounds ($324.9 million) to 450 million pounds, chief executive Peter Davis told Reuters that the company had now made offers in 30 percent of all priority cases.
Davis also said that the search for a branch network, while still on the agenda, was on the back burner.

"What we wanted to do was speed up the whole review process and so we made the decision to stop arguing about whether the Pru was at fault and in those priority cases where the customer was disadvantaged, to make it up," said Davis.
At the end of May, the Pru had made offers in 3,000 of priority cases, a figure that had since risen to 16,000.
The decision to guarantee the benefits people would have had if they had remained in occupational schemes was the main reason for the steep increase in the group's provisions, Davis said.
Changes to advanced corporation tax in the budget had added another 35 million pounds to the bill.
He said the company would report regularly on provisions in the future.
"Its a bit of a moving feast. This is our best estimate today on what is necessary for the priority cases," said Davis.

But the rise in provisions will not hit profits which in the first six months of the year rose to 442 million pounds from 421 million pounds. Excluding income from disposals, profits from continuing operations were up 19 percent.
Davis said he was very happy with the performance.
"Last year we had the M&G reinsurance business. We said when we sold it, it would be dilutive but we've actually been able to make that up in operating performance in the rest of the group," he said.
Davis reiterated the group's desire to improve access to customers and confirmed the group was still looking for a branch network.
The Pru had failed to find the right solution at the right price, he said.
"Building societies are very expensive. A branch network is still on the agenda but it is on the back burner."
But he refused to be drawn on reports that the group had been in talks with National Westminster Bank about a possible merger.

"Inevitably in this business, when its going through change and the industry's going through change, you talk to a number of people, but none of the discussions reached a level that was worth reporting," said Davis.
The group would only do a deal that added value to sahareholders, he stressed.
In the UK the company's objectives remain to expand its product range and distribution capabilities and building its customer base.
Prudential UK profits rose 16 percent to 197 million pounds with a nine percent increase in life pension and investment business to 170 million pounds.
Prudential banking, launched on October 1 last year, has since attracted 250 million pounds of mortgage applications and 274 million pounds of deposits and remained on target, Davis said.

The U.S. had another good year with profits from Jackson National Life up 15 percent to 176 million pounds. Excluding currency factors, profits were up 23 percent and Davis expressed himself well pleased with the performance.
"Its a very good business and I'm confident we'll continue to show progress there," he said.
Funds under management around the world reached 100 billion pounds, a figure which will rise to 110 billion pounds once the Scottish Amicable acquisition is completed in September.
-- Simon Cowell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7721 ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
